PullRequest.Title: AgentHost - add multi-root support for the checkpoint service
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after behavior, subprocess implementations, and downstream pair-equality fast path are all explicit in the diff and call chain; only exact wall-clock magnitude varies by repository and platform.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses, checkpoint refs/commit objects, and the subsequent git-diff subprocess
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The extra commit/ref and later diff are incurred once per repository for every completed turn whose captured tree is unchanged; retained refs/commits grow with no-op turn count until session cleanup.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased end-of-turn changeset latency and subprocess/I/O load, plus avoidable Git object/ref growth during long sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The deleted implementation resolved the parent tree, reused the parent ref when the tree was identical, and returned without commit-tree/update-ref; AgentHostChangesetService also recognizes parent === current and skips git diff entirely.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every successfully captured tree now unconditionally runs commit-tree and update-ref and records a fresh turn ref, even when that tree equals the parent tree.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 144 adds unconditional commitTree after the PR deletes the parent-tree equality branch that previously returned the parent ref for an unchanged tree.
Findings.Title: Restore the no-op checkpoint fast path
Findings.Impact: Read-only or conversational turns with no repository edits now create a redundant commit/ref per repository and force changeset computation through git diff before publishing the final changeset. Long sessions with many such turns accumulate refs and repeatedly spawn avoidable git processes.
Findings.Evidence: captureWorkingTreeAsTree already returns a tree OID, but the added line commits it without comparing it to `${parentCommitOid}^{tree}`. The removed hunk explicitly performed that comparison and persisted parentRef on equality. The unchanged _computeTurnDiffsPreferCheckpoint fast path returns [] only when pair.parent === pair.current; fresh refs defeat it. commitTree/updateRef/computeFileDiffsBetweenRefs each invoke git subprocesses in AgentHostGitService.
Findings.Recommendation: Compare each captured tree with its parent before creating commits. If all repositories are unchanged, persist the previous ref so parent === current remains true; if another repository requires a new shared ref name, point unchanged repositories at the parent commit without creating redundant commits.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The folder-to-root normalization, repeated repository-wide subprocess chain, sequential await ordering, and changeset dependency are directly traced. The only magnitude uncertainty is how often users include multiple workspace folders from one repository.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses and temporary index filesystem operations used to capture and commit a full repository tree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost scales with configured working-directory count rather than unique repository count; N workspace folders within one repository repeat the same sequential full-tree capture N times per turn.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher end-of-turn latency and avoidable CPU, subprocess, and filesystem I/O, delaying final changeset publication.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Checkpoint capture accepted only the primary working directory, so one turn could execute this full repository capture at most once.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new multi-root loop resolves each working directory and immediately performs baseline lookup, parent lookup, full working-tree capture, commit-tree, and update-ref, without grouping equal repository roots.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 117 introduces iteration over every supplied working directory; the subsequent added body performs repository-wide Git work for each entry with no root-level deduplication.
Findings.Title: Deduplicate working directories by repository root
Findings.Impact: A realistic multi-root workspace containing sibling folders or a repository plus one of its subfolders resolves multiple entries to the same Git root. Each completed turn then serially captures and commits that same repository once per folder before AgentSideEffects can invoke changesets.onTurnComplete.
Findings.Evidence: getRepositoryRoot canonicalizes each folder to its Git top level. captureWorkingTreeAsTree then runs git status, creates a temporary index directory, runs read-tree/staging/write-tree, and the caller follows with commit-tree/update-ref. The loop is sequential and has no Set keyed by repositoryRootUri, while AgentSideEffects waits for captureTurnCheckpoint to settle before scheduling the final changeset.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve all working directories to repository roots first, deduplicate by canonical URI, then run baseline/turn capture once per unique repository while preserving the current per-repository best-effort error handling.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The review-ref cleanup listener looked up its working directory from live session state after AgentService had already deleted that state, so disposed reviewed sessions retained their refs indefinitely in the repository.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: One reviewed Git ref leaked per disposed reviewed session, causing repository ref/object retention and progressively more ref namespace work over time.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The deletion event now carries working directories captured before teardown, and the review cleanup consumes them directly to delete the reviewed ref before session data/worktree removal.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision AgentService called stateManager.deleteSession before deleteSessionData fired the review listener; base line 234 then queried the now-removed session state and returned without deleteRefs. The PR captures effective working directories before teardown, forwards them through deleteSessionData, and line 58 passes them into disposal, making ref cleanup reachable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Materializing a Git-backed Copilot session captures baseline checkpoints for all resolved working directories.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session metadata is awaited, but baseline capture is fire-and-forget before the materialize event, so its Git work is off the immediate materialization return path; the per-session sequencer can make it precede a later turn checkpoint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository root, verify baseline ref, capture a full working tree through status/read-tree/staging/write-tree, commit-tree, and update-ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold successful capture runs once per effective repository; multiple folders resolving to one repository still pay root/ref checks, while subsequent duplicate folders skip the full capture after seeing the new baseline ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the primary working directory was captured, so at most one repository incurred the baseline subprocess chain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate materialization return path, but serialized ahead of later checkpoint work for that session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/delete a temporary index directory and stage changed paths while constructing the checkpoint tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per repository that lacks a baseline and captures successfully.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operation existed for the single primary repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same off-path baseline task, but can delay queued per-session checkpoint operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured working-directory count, with effective cardinality intended to be unique Git repositories but currently equal to directory entries until baseline refs make duplicate roots skip later work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Directories are processed serially inside one session; the SequencerByKey serializes baseline/turn/deletion work per session, while different sessions have no shared Git concurrency limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository-root lookups have a positive in-memory cache per input directory; baseline existence is checked with git rev-parse on every attempted capture, and failures are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call ordering, serial loop, cache behavior, and Git/file operations are directly implemented.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace root counts and repository sizes vary; the subprocess and temporary-index mechanisms are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Multi-root fan-out is required, but repository-root grouping is needed to keep work proportional to unique repositories; this is covered by a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Completing an agent turn captures checkpoints before publishing final changesets.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Queued-message draining and host notification do not wait, but changesets.onTurnComplete is invoked only after captureTurnCheckpoint settles, so all sequential checkpoint work is on the final changeset publication path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For each directory, run repository/ref resolution, full working-tree capture, commit-tree, and update-ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One chain per working-directory entry per uncaptured turn, even when entries resolve to the same repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One chain was run for the single persisted working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the final turn changeset recomputation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute final per-turn Git diff between checkpoint refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for an observed/final turn when parent and current refs differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged trees reused the parent ref, so parent === current bypassed this subprocess; the PR's unconditional fresh checkpoint defeats that fast path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks changeset publication after checkpoint capture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/remove temporary index directories and stage changed files for each tree capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per loop entry and completed uncaptured turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Occurred once for the primary repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of checkpoint latency before changeset scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Completed turn count times configured directories; effective cardinality should be unique repositories, and no-op turns are common realistic inputs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All repositories are awaited serially in a per-session sequencer. Different sessions can run concurrently without a shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive repository-root lookups are cached by input directory. Baseline and parent refs are verified with uncached git rev-parse calls; checkpoint capture itself is not cached beyond the database's turn-ref idempotence check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the unconditional commit/ref path, removed equality branch, duplicate-root fan-out, and downstream pair-equality shortcut are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact Git duration depends on repository size, changed/untracked paths, filesystem, and root count; the added multiplicity and no-op work are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two actionable regressions were reported: loss of no-op ref reuse and lack of repository-root deduplication.

Scenarios.Scenario: Computing subscribed, compare-turn, and static changesets reads checkpoint pairs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkpoint-pair and baseline lookups must finish before Git diff or fallback diff computation and before publishing the requested changeset.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Verify the deterministic baseline ref with git rev-parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per getTurnCheckpointPair, plus a parallel direct baseline lookup for static session changesets; compare-turn can issue two.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Baseline ref was read from session database metadata without a Git subprocess.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Diff parent/current refs when a valid non-equal pair is returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per requested changeset computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same Git diff boundary existed, with no-op pairs bypassing it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per recomputation; compare-turn requests issue two pair lookups, while static session changesets request baseline and pair concurrently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all parallelizes paired metadata/baseline lookups; per-URI diff recomputations are sequenced elsewhere.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Turn refs remain database-backed, but baseline existence is now an uncached git rev-parse; repository roots are positively cached when later diff APIs resolve them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundary change; lower magnitude than the reported repeated full-tree and no-op paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Recompute frequency depends on subscriptions and edit bursts; the added ref verification is bounded per computation.
Scenarios.Verdict: The extra baseline verification adds bounded subprocess overhead, but the reviewed evidence does not justify a separate finding beyond the reported no-op path's additional diff fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disposing a session cleans review/checkpoint refs, deletes session data, then removes an isolated worktree.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider disposal completes first; SessionDataService then waits for checkpoint and review cleanup promises before recursive data deletion, and AgentService waits for that before worktree removal and final state teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve roots and batch-delete checkpoint/review refs with git update-ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Checkpoint and review cleanup each issue up to one batched delete per working-directory entry/repository; duplicate roots can add checks, though checkpoint deletion skips after the first removes baseline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Checkpoint cleanup targeted one persisted repository; review cleanup attempted one live-state lookup but deterministically no-op'd after state deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks session data deletion and worktree removal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively delete the per-session data directory and remove any isolated worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deletions occurred in the opposite order, after live session state teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both are awaited by disposeSession; data deletion now precedes worktree removal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured working directories and accumulated turn refs; refs are batched per repository, while directory loops are serial within each cleanup service.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Checkpoint and review listeners are awaited together via Promise.allSettled; each listener serially processes directories, and checkpoint work is sequenced per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository-root positive cache can avoid repeated rev-parse by input directory. Checkpoint refs are loaded once from the database; baseline existence is checked per repository. No retained per-session cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: lifecycle ordering and awaited boundaries are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cleanup duration depends on root count, ref history, and worktree size; the prior review-ref leak and fixed ordering are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: The new ordering fixes an unbounded review-ref retention regression and was recorded as a regression fix; no new disposal-path finding met the reporting threshold.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 15 changed files and traced baseline capture, turn completion/changeset publication, checkpoint reads, and disposal across Git subprocess and filesystem boundaries. Submitted two medium-confidence-high performance findings and recorded the cleanup-lifecycle regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
